claim: The PR has no description at all, although it is a `perf` change that also alters the public signature of `Mathlib.Tactic.addRelatedDecl` and `elementwiseExpr` and changes what the generated `_assoc`/`_apply`/`_app` proofs look like (they now reference the source constant instead of inlining its proof term). A reviewer has to reconstruct the motivation and the safety argument from the diff, and there is no measurement backing the `perf` title.
requested_change: Write a description that (a) states the motivation: `addRelatedDecl` passed `info.value!` to `construct`, so every derived lemma re-embedded the source's full proof and the kernel re-checked it; (b) states the design choice: `construct` now receives `.const src levelParams` and infers the type itself, which is why the `type` argument and the `mkExpectedTypeHint` calls go away; (c) reports `!bench` (or equivalent) numbers so the perf claim is measured; (d) flags the breaking change to `addRelatedDecl`'s `construct` signature and `elementwiseExpr`'s arguments for downstream users; (e) says whether AI assistance was used, per the contribution policy.

claim: The point of the PR is a property of the generated proof terms: the derived lemma should reference the source constant instead of copying its proof. No existing test checks this. The tests only check that the generated statements elaborate and are usable, so a later refactor could bring back the duplicated proof without anything failing.
